title: 1:1 prep - Alicia Park (CSM) & Avery Chen - Atlas Payments - 2026-03-04
body:
Meeting: 1:1 prep notes for weekly sync with Alicia Park (CSM)
Date/Time: 2026-03-04 10:00am PT (30m)
Account: Atlas Payments (mid-market fintech)
ARR: $420k (expands to $1.2M post-rollout)
Renewal window: 2026-09 (Q3)
Primary contacts: Alicia Park (CSM), Michael Hsu (Head of AI), Raj Patel (Infra lead)
Recent context: rollout of Redwood Dedicated started Feb; initial latency issues on high-concurrency flows fixed by Maya last week (patch 0.9.3). Michael flagged cost uptick vs proj baseline; finance raised question about token usage on reconciliation job. Two support tickets last month (CS-1109: streaming timeouts; CS-1118: unexpected decoding artifact) — both resolved but resurfacing concerns during sit-downs.

Top goals for this 1:1
- Align on account health signals and escalation plan if cost/latency trend continues
- Prep for upcoming QBR (w/AE Tomas) — identify 3 wins + 2 asks (budget + technical)
- Review open action items from previous sync and confirm owners/dates

Agenda (30m)
1) Quick sync (5m) — How is Alicia feeling about account health? any new exec asks?
2) Incidents & support lift (7m) — recap tickets, residual impact, SRE/SE follow-ups (Maya)
3) QBR prep (10m) — wins, metrics to pull, slides required, who presents which section
4) Actions & next steps (8m) — owners, timing, what I handle vs Alicia/Tomas/Maya

Notes / Talking points to surface
- Cost: Michael said last week's run increased monthly token spend ~18% over plan (recon jobs). Quick wins: enable prefix caching on reconciliation pipeline (SE task), review batching strategy (suggested by Optimize). Ask Tomas to surface possible committed discount options for Dedicated customers approaching $1M ARR.
- Latency: overall P95 dropped after 0.9.3 but tail latency still spikes under concurrency >200; Maya to validate kernel selection telemetry and share dashboard links.
- Adoption: 6/8 internal teams actively using generation endpoints; fraud-team still in POC. Need case study + 1 pager to unblock exec sponsorship.
- Support backlog: confirm CS-1118 root cause (tokenization edge-case) permanently fixed or needs patch rollout. If patch required, propose canary to small subset.
- QBR asks: (1) pilot dedicated autoscaling policy (60-day trial), (2) one-time credits to offset cost variance while optimizing (ask finance/sales to consider).

Data to pull before QBR (Avery asks Tomas/Alicia to help pull):
- Month-over-month token spend by top 3 pipelines (recon, fraud, invoices) — get last 6 weeks
- Latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) for gen endpoints by workload
- Error rates and support ticket summary (last 90 days)
- Adoption heatmap: number of active users per team + key success stories

Open action items (from last 1:1) — status check
- Maya: validate kernel selection telemetry + share Grafana dashboard (due: 2026-03-03) — status: reported fixed for some flows, still investigating tail spikes.
- Tomas: draft QBR slide outline and suggested commercial ask (due: 2026-03-05) — status: started; needs input on credits ask.
- Alicia: collect two internal use-cases to highlight during QBR (due: 2026-03-08) — status: has one (invoices), chasing fraud-team.

New action items (to confirm in meeting)
- [Alicia] Confirm exec attendee list for QBR and get Michael Hsu's availability (due: 2026-03-07)
- [Tomas] Pull token spend by pipeline + propose commercial credits/discount ask for review (due: 2026-03-05)
- [Maya] Deep-dive on tail latency: produce short doc with findings and mitigation plan + timeline for patch (due: 2026-03-10)
- [Avery] Draft 1-pager case study for fraud-team to accelerate sponsorship (due: 2026-03-06)
- [Avery/Tomas] Prepare QBR slide deck skeleton: 6 slides (exec summary, adoption, ops & reliability, cost, roadmap + asks, next steps) (due: 2026-03-09)

Risks & mitigation
- Risk: Cost overruns could trigger procurement pushback and delay dedicated expansion. Mitigation: short-term credits + technical optimizations (cache/batching) to show cost delta within 30 days.
- Risk: Tail latency impacts SLOs and may erode trust. Mitigation: canary rollback plan and SRE on-call rotation for QBR week.

Questions to ask Alicia in meeting
- Any escalations outside Michael we need I loop into? (finance/legal?)
- Is fraud-team's blocker technical or organizational? Do they need a short joint workshop with SE?
- Are there internal timelines pushing for a capex vs opex decision this quarter?

Prep checklist for me (Avery) before meeting
- Pull latest billing snapshot (ask Billing/Finance) — attach to QBR deck
- Jot one-line wins for each active team (invoices, reconciliation, support, fraud)
- Review CS-1118 ticket thread to confirm fix and next steps
- Draft the 1-pager template for fraud team case study (to send live in meeting for Alicia to edit)

Tone / coaching notes for 1:1 with Alicia
- Empathize with cost sensitivity; lead with quick technical wins and timeline to show impact
- Be collaborative on commercial ask (present it as temporary bridge while we optimize)
- Push for concrete commitments (dates/owners) she can take to Michael

Follow-up plan after 1:1
- Send meeting notes + action item list (I own) within 24h
- Trigger a short sync with Tomas and Maya to stitch technical + commercial ask into deck
- Schedule QBR dry-run 48h before presentation

Quick wins to drive this week
- Turn on prefix caching for recon job (SE) — expected ~10-20% token reduction
- Short audit of prompt lengths in reconciliation flow (Avery) — flag top 5 offenders
- Build one slide showing cost vs baseline projection with/without caching

Misc scratch notes (to keep)
- Potential hook: show Redwood Optimize suggestions estimate in $, make commercial ask smaller
- Check if Dedicated committed tiers have an unused buffer we can temporarily use
- Slack threads: #cs-atlas-payments and #redwood-dedicated-ops

-- end of prep notes
